report.summary: Chunk 2 of ignore.py: defines _fingerprint, load_ignore_rules, env_extra_patterns, _norm_center, ProjectScope dataclass with center_of, in_center, is_shell, describe, and fingerprint property.
risks: load_ignore_rules / high / Missing/unreadable file returns empty rules but does not differentiate between missing and unreadable; caller may not know which. / Add a distinct fingerprint or flag for unreadable vs missing.
todos: Verify that load_ignore_rules handles non-OSError exceptions (e.g., PermissionError) as intended; currently only catches OSError.

handoff.purpose: Define ignore rule loading, environment pattern fetching, path normalization, and ProjectScope dataclass with center/shell logic.

symbols.name: _fingerprint
symbols.note: Returns first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of text.

symbols.name: load_ignore_rules
symbols.note: Reads .daedalusignore, returns IgnoreRules; empty if file missing/unreadable.

symbols.name: env_extra_patterns
symbols.note: Returns list of patterns from DAEDALUS_IGNORE env var, split by os.pathsep.

symbols.name: _norm_center
symbols.note: Normalizes center paths to repo-relative POSIX, sorted, deduplicated.

symbols.name: ProjectScope
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with center tuple and ignore IgnoreRules.

symbols.name: ProjectScope.in_center
symbols.note: Returns True if rel equals or starts with any center root; empty center returns True.

symbols.name: ProjectScope.center_of
symbols.note: Returns the longest matching center root for rel, or None.

symbols.name: ProjectScope.is_shell
symbols.note: True if rel is outside center or matched by ignore rules.

symbols.name: ProjectScope.describe
symbols.note: Returns dict with center list and ignore patterns.

claims.text: The fingerprint covers the raw file bytes and is folded into the index cache key by ``cached_index``. Without that, editing the ignore file would hand back the previous process-cached index and look like the feature simply did not work.
claims.why: The docstring refers to `cached_index` and process-caching behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``DAEDALUS_IGNORE`` -- os.pathsep-separated patterns, applied after the file. Exists so a scan can be scoped without editing a tracked file.
claims.why: Code splits os.environ['DAEDALUS_IGNORE'] by os.pathsep and returns list of non-empty stripped patterns.

claims.text: Normalise center paths to repo-relative POSIX, no leading/trailing '/'.
claims.why: Code replaces backslashes with forward slashes, strips '/', and excludes '.' and empty strings.

claims.text: Sorted + de-duplicated: this feeds the cache fingerprint, so two configs that name the same roots in a different order must not build twice.
claims.why: Code returns `tuple(sorted(set(out)))` ensuring uniqueness and consistent order.

claims.text: An empty center means the whole repo is the core, which is the historical behaviour and what every un-configured repo keeps getting.

NOT expressible as ``in_center``: that returns True for every path when no center is declared (the whole repo is the core), which is right for metric decisions and actively wrong for naming ones. A caller written as ``if scope.in_center(rel): strip_prefix(rel)`` would read as "strip everything" on an unconfigured repo and only no-op by accident. This returns None there, so "no center -> no package root -> no stripping" falls out structurally instead of coincidentally.
claims.why: `center_of` returns None when no center matches; `in_center` returns True for empty center. The code matches the described behavior.

claims.text: LONGEST MATCH WINS, not first-sorted. With ``center=["a", "a/b"]`` the file ``a/b/c.py`` lives in the *inner* package root, so its package-relative name is ``c`` and not ``b.c``. Ties are impossible: two centers that both match and have equal length are the same string, and ``_norm_center`` already de-duplicated. Sorted before the length sort so the iteration order is total and never depends on config ordering.
claims.why: Code sorts `self.center` lexicographically, then iterates updating `best` when len(c) > len(best). Longest match wins. De-duplication from _norm_center ensures ties are impossible.

claims.text: True when ``rel`` is indexed-but-peripheral: outside the declared center, or matched by an ignore rule. These are the files withheld from metrics and not expanded through.
claims.why: Code returns `(not self.in_center(rel)) or self.ignore.matches(rel)`, exactly matching the description.

observations.what: load_ignore_rules catches OSError but not other exceptions like PermissionError (which is a subclass of OSError in Python 3.3+). Actually PermissionError is a subclass of OSError, so it is caught. However, other exceptions like UnicodeDecodeError (if errors='replace' fails?) or MemoryError are not handled. But errors='replace' should prevent decode errors. Still, the docstring says 'Missing/unreadable file -> empty rules', which matches OSError only.
ProjectScope.describe returns a dict with ignore_patterns list; the patterns are formatted with '!' prefix for negated, pattern, and '/' suffix for dir_only. This matches typical .gitignore style.
